title: Space Attack — Codex game-build conversation export
scope: Initial game request through the final canvas-size commit and successful deployment (264470d), on 2 October 2026.
source: Actual user and assistant text from the locally saved Codex session; not a reconstructed summary or native Share URL.

messages.text: I will paste you a task description - basically create a galaxian clone - let's do this in typescript - and probably use the phaser 3 library
Paste the task description, and I’ll build it in TypeScript with Phaser 3, using the existing project as a starting point.

The task: build Space Attack, a small, polished browser arcade game where the player pilots a spaceship against waves of enemies. Reference: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jYIC8ADIArc

It must include:

Keyboard movement and firing, with on-screen instructions
Enemy waves, working collisions, a visible score and health/lives
Increasing difficulty
A start screen, game over and restart
I’ll inspect the project and the reference, then build a playable Phaser 3 game with wave progression, clear controls, and polished start and game-over screens.

The project is empty, so I’m setting up TypeScript, Vite, and Phaser 3. The video couldn’t be fetched; I’ll use the Galaxian-style mechanics you described: enemy formations, diving attacks, and increasingly fast waves, with a neon arcade look.

let's make it a little more interesting too - some enemies take multiple hits - the colour can change to indicate how many hits left - green -> orange -> red (or just orange -> red) only add those after 2 or three levels - 2 hits first then a couple of levels later the 3 hit versions
I’ll introduce two-hit enemies on wave 3, then three-hit enemies on wave 5. Their colour will show remaining health: green → orange → red, with red enemies always one hit from destruction.

The game mechanics and screens are implemented, including armour colour changes on waves 3 and 5. I’ve also added pause, optional sound effects, touch controls, and a saved best score. I’m checking the build and browser gameplay now.

The TypeScript check and production build pass. The game is running at `http://localhost:5173/`. No browser is connected in this session, so I couldn’t visually verify it or play-test the controls and collisions.

Built with TypeScript and Phaser 3. Play at [localhost:5173](http://localhost:5173/).

Includes movement, firing, diving enemies, collisions, score, three lives, increasing difficulty, start/game-over/restart screens, pause, sound, and touch controls.

- Wave 3: two-hit enemies, orange → red.
- Wave 5: three-hit enemies, green → orange → red.

`npm run build` passes. Browser play-testing remains unverified because no browser is connected.

ok - first version is looking pretty good - let's add more alien varieties - also increase the canvas size - it's a bit small - decrease the speed and number of aliens on the first level and increase as we progress
I’ll enlarge the playfield, add distinct alien designs, and make wave 1 smaller and slower, with enemy count and speed building across later waves.
commit the first draft before continuing
I’ll commit the first draft now, before making the canvas, alien variety, or difficulty changes.
Committed the first draft as `f1cdfbd`. I’m continuing with the larger playfield and gentler opening wave; those changes will remain separate from that commit.

The first draft is safely committed. The updated playfield is 1200 × 720, with a wider page layout. Wave 1 now starts with 12 aliens instead of 30, moving and attacking more slowly. Four alien designs have distinct flight patterns, while their colours still indicate remaining health.

First draft committed as `f1cdfbd`.

The subsequent changes are implemented and uncommitted:

- Larger 1200 × 720 playfield and wider layout.
- Four alien varieties with different flight patterns.
- Slower wave 1 with 12 aliens; later waves increase count and speed.
- Armour progression remains on waves 3 and 5.

Build and progression checks pass. Refresh [the game](http://localhost:5173/) to try it.

ok - make the aliens have more left right movement - some can sweep across the screen - also when they get past the player and re-appear - make them come down from the top of the screen - not just 'appear'
I’ll give the aliens wider side-to-side paths, including full-screen sweeps, and make enemies that pass the player fly back in from above the screen.

Updated:

- Wider side-to-side formation movement and individual weaving.
- Some aliens sweep across the screen, bouncing at the edges.
- Escaping aliens now descend from above the screen and smoothly rejoin formation.

Build and movement checks pass. Refresh [the game](http://localhost:5173/) to try it.
commit
I’ll commit the canvas, alien variety, difficulty, and movement updates together.

Committed as `106db3e` — expanded playfield, alien varieties, progressive difficulty, sweeping attacks, and smooth re-entry.

Working tree is clean.
ok - let's add polish up the graphics a little - less pixel arty - let's go fo a more mature cartoon look

I’ll redraw the ship and aliens with smoother silhouettes, shaded bodies, and expressive details for a more mature cartoon style. I’ll keep the health colours and distinct alien shapes easy to read during play.

The new artwork is in place: shaded hulls, cockpit glass, organic alien shapes, and expressive eyes. I’ve also added a flickering engine plume, gentle ship banking, and softer projectile and impact effects. I’m checking the artwork and build now.

Updated with smooth, shaded cartoon artwork: expressive aliens, a detailed ship with cockpit glass, animated engine exhaust, gentle banking, and softer weapon effects.

Health colours remain clear. Build passes, and I visually checked all alien designs and colour variants.

Refresh [the game](http://localhost:5173/) to try it. Changes are uncommitted.

Fixed—the SVG URLs I added used percent encoding, but Phaser’s loader expects base64.

All 15 artwork assets now pass through Phaser’s actual loader without decoding errors, and the build passes. Refresh the game to try again.
ok - good - commit that
I’ll commit the graphics polish and SVG loading fix together.

Committed as `b844973` — cartoon graphics polish and SVG loading fix.

Working tree is clean.

ok - now let's change the font sizes to be a little bigger - the instructions etc are hard to read - whilst we're at it let's also change the narrative around the game a little - we're defending earth against an alien invasion - the future of humanity is at stake!  let's add a 'wormhole' that the initial alien formation arrive from at the start of each level and update the text around the game to reflect this
I’ll increase the instruction and interface text sizes, rewrite the game around defending Earth, and add a wormhole entrance that brings each wave into formation.

The Earth-defence story is now reflected in the start screen, mission status, pause, and game-over text. Instructions are up to 16px with better contrast. Each wave now emerges from a rotating wormhole and fans out into formation before attacks begin; I’ve also added a subtle Earth horizon behind the player.

Updated:

- Larger, higher-contrast instructions and interface text.
- Earth-defence narrative throughout the game.
- A rotating wormhole that releases each wave into formation before attacks begin.
- A subtle Earth horizon behind the player.

Build, SVG loading, and arrival-path checks pass. Refresh [the game](http://localhost:5173/) to try it. Changes are uncommitted.

ok - move the wormhole to the top left and persist it's view - it should 'engorge' when the aliens deploy before shrinking once they aliens are through - let's also improve the missile graphics a little

I’ll move the wormhole to the top left and keep it visible between waves, expanding as aliens deploy and shrinking afterward. I’ll also give the missiles clearer bodies, glowing tips, and exhaust trails.
no need for exhaust tails
Got it—no exhaust trails. I’ll focus the missile polish on their bodies and glowing tips, alongside the persistent wormhole animation.

The wormhole now stays visible in the top-left corner. It swells and pulses during deployment, then contracts to a smaller idle size. Player and alien missiles now have distinct shaded bodies and glowing tips, with no exhaust trails. The loading and movement checks pass.

Done—the wormhole stays visible at the top left, expands during alien deployment, then shrinks afterward.

Missiles now have shaded bodies and glowing tips, without exhaust trails.

Build and loading/movement checks pass. Refresh [the game](http://localhost:5173/) to try it. Changes remain uncommitted.
we also need to add details on how to run it to the README (add separate sections for Linux/Windows/Mac if relevant) - commit the previous work first
I’ll commit the current game changes first, then add setup and run instructions to the README for Linux, Windows, and macOS.

The game changes are committed as `688a4b5`. The README now has separate Linux, Windows, and macOS instructions, plus prerequisites, production builds, and troubleshooting. It also covers the `npm.cmd` workaround for PowerShell script restrictions.

Committed the previous game work as `688a4b5`.

ok - now let's add a background star field - it can be quite sparse and shouldn't distract from the gameplay - also the sounds are very basic - let's see if we can improve them a little - commit the readme work first
I’ll commit the README update first, then add a subtle star field and improve the firing, impact, and wave-transition sounds.

The sound effects now have distinct layers for weapon fire, armour hits, explosions, shield damage, and wave transitions, with softer envelopes and a master compressor to control overlapping sounds.

README committed as `8e10f78`.

Added a sparse, slowly drifting star field and richer effects for weapons, impacts, explosions, damage, and wave transitions.

Build and audio checks pass. Refresh [the game](http://localhost:5173/) and enable **SOUND ON** to try them. New changes remain uncommitted.

ok - the starfield doesn't really look like anything - let's park it for now - commit the current work - then i want to also add some limited up and down movement for more varied evasion - let's allow movement up to a third of the screen - let's also add a difficulty level picker (easy - medium - hard)

Medium keeps the current balance; Easy has fewer, slower enemies, and Hard has more enemies with faster movement and attacks. I’m also separating best scores by difficulty.

ok - let's get that committed  - next - let's cap this at 10 levels - for the final level let's have a big boss alien - defended by normal ones - give it a health bar requiring ultiple hits to defeat - once killed add a victory jingle and congraulatory message

Previous changes committed as `f997bca`.
